feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. (1) In iteration 0 the 4 cm, 5-sensor array at a 5 cm lead gave 1-2 line-loss events per run and every run went off track at 10-15% progress (entityR2B). The line leaves the array on bends. (2) In iteration 1 the wider 6 cm, 5-sensor array at a 4 cm lead cut line losses to 1 per run, but all 60 runs still went off track at 11-16% progress, with max_error 0.061-0.066 m (entityR2B). Widening the span helped but did not solve the drift, so the remaining limits are the span and the lead. (3) Oscillation stayed low at 0.07-0.155 across both iterations, so the sensor spacing is not causing jitter. (4) For the controller, the weights x/0.03 keep the same slope as iteration 1, so kp 3.0 and kd 0.1 carry over. A closer lead needs slightly more damping, so I raised kd to 0.15 in the package. Next race: if line_loss_events is 0 but the robot still goes off track, the lead is probably too far forward for the bend, so try y = 0.02 m. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 while line losses stay at 0, reduce sensor_size to 0.012 or raise kd. If the signal looks too weak at the outer sensors (line losses still occur at the ±6 cm extremes), narrow the span to ±5 cm.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is 0 but the robot still goes off track, move the lead from y = 0.03 m to y = 0.02 m. Iteration 0 (5 cm lead) and iteration 1 (4 cm lead) both gave off-track exits at 11-16% progress with line losses, so the lead is still the most likely limit.

If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.15 while line_loss_events stays 0, reduce sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m to shrink the footprint overlap. Iteration 1 showed oscillation of 0.07-0.155, so this only applies if the new array raises it.

If line losses remain above 0 at the outer sensors (x = ±0.06 m), narrow the span to ±0.05 m with 2 cm pitch (x = -0.05, -0.03, -0.01, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05 for six sensors, or equivalent seven-sensor spacing). Iteration 1 showed a 6 cm span still losing the line once per run, so the outer sensors may be too far from the tape.
